newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH INVESTORS BULLISH ON STOCKS - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH INVESTORS BULLISH ON STOCKS - PAPER.

text.p: Finnish professional investors are bullish on the stock market outlook, business daily Kauppalehti reported on Thursday.

"Investors' expectations for the trend in share prices are the most optimistic in one and a half year," it said, citing an opinion poll among 51 professional investors conducted by Suomen Gallup Markkinatutkimus Oy on behalf of itself and the Finnish Foundation for Share Promotion.
Of those polled, 88 percent said share prices would rise in the coming six months. The mean of their forecasts for the HEX all-share index in March 1997 was 2,207 points.
The HEX index closed at 2,104.36 on Wednesday.
Sixty percent of investors expected bourse-listed companies' net results to fall this year on 1995. Net results would fall by on average 15 percent, according to the mean of their forecasts.
But three of four respondents expected results to improve in 1997.

Asked about prospects for various categories of shares on the Helsinki Stock Exchange, 37 percent of investors said the forest industry would rise most, 18 percent believed in banks and as many said metal and engineering industry shares would perform best.
Two thirds of investors said they would buy Nokia shares while one third said they would not, Kauppalehti reported.
Next to Nokia, the most popular shares on investors' autumn shopping lists were Enso , Merita , Metra and UPM-Kymmene .
Leading the list of stocks to sell were Amer , Merita and Raision Tehtaat .
